title: Fetchlinks post record (contract v2)
description: Version 1 plus the identity of the origin that carried the post. A post's unique_id is a digest of its URL set, so the same article legitimately arrives more than once from different places; these four fields are what tells those arrivals apart. Version 1 remains valid and readable -- this is an addition, not a correction.

unique_id.description: Natural deduplication key derived from the post's sorted URLs.

source.description: Human-meaningful origin of the post, e.g. a site or subreddit URL.

source_type.description: Collector that produced the record. A free-form lowercase token so a new source needs no contract change.

direct_link.description: Permalink to the post itself. Empty when the source has no distinct permalink.

channel_key.description: Stable identity of the place the post appeared: the feed's own URL, the subreddit name, the Mastodon instance. Must survive a rename of anything cosmetic, because ratings are attached to it. Empty when the source has no such dimension, as with the Bluesky timeline.

channel_label.description: Display name for the channel. Never used as identity.

actor_key.description: Stable identity of the account that posted: a Bluesky DID, a Mastodon account URI, a Reddit username. Deliberately not a display name, which is renameable. Empty when the source has no author, as with an RSS feed.

actor_label.description: Display name for the actor. Never used as identity.

urls.description: External URLs in collection order. Array position is the authoritative ordering.
